articleTitle: Dose Effects on Bipolar Transistors Belonging to a CMOS SOI Process
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The Total Ionizing Dose response of bipolar transistors, manufactured with a CMOS SOI process is presented. Both base and collector currents increase with TID. TCAD simulation is used to explain the observed experimental results.

articleTitle: Measurement of Total Ionizing Dose Effects on SiC Trench MOSFETs by Gamma-ray and Alpha-particle Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We measured total ionizing dose effect (TID) on Si, SiC planar and SiC trench power MOSFETs by using Co-60 $\gamma$-ray source and 241Am $\alpha$-particle source. Measurement results show that SiC power MOSFETs have higher tolerance to $\gamma$-ray irradiation. In contrast, the SiC trench MOSFET is most vulnerable to $\alpha$-particle-induced TID. Threshold voltage shift, $\triangle V_{\mathrm{t}\mathrm{h}}$ of the SiC trench MOSFET is -4.SV after 150 krad $\alpha$-particle irradiation, which is 12.6% larger than that in the Si MOSFET. In this measurements, the SiC planar MOSFET has the highest tolerance for both $\alpha$-particle and $\gamma$-ray irradiation. $\Delta V_{\mathrm{t}\mathrm{h}}$ of the SiC planar MOSFET is 1/20 or less than that of the Si MOSFET.

articleTitle: Photocurrent of Substrate PNP Bipolar Transistor Submitted to Pulsed X-ray Irradiation: The Influence of Neutron Displacement Damage
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The influence of neutron displacement damage on the amplitude and duration time of primary and secondary photocurrent of SPNP transistor under pulsed X-ray irradiation are investigated thoroughly at various neutron fluence and transient dose rates.

articleTitle: Radiation-induced Enhancement of Scattering Effects in FD-SOI MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Experimental results show a radiation response in 22 nm fully depleted silicon on insulator (FDSOI) transistors to 10 keVx-rays. A degradation in the mobility is observed as a function of radiation. The mobility degradation is shown to be position dependent by testing at different back gate biases. The method used to extract mobility from drain current is shown. Quantum mechanical simulations were performed to show the shift in the charge centroid with varying back gate bias.

articleTitle: Single Bit Upsets versus Burst Errors of Stacked-Capacitor DRAMs Induced by High-Energy Neutron - SECDED is No Longer Effective -
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We measured soft errors on two 8Gb DRAMs by neutron irradiation. The results showed that the soft error rates for both DRAMs were about 3 FIT/Gb. An SBU that can be corrected by ECC were rarely measured, while burst errors caused by soft errors on peripheral circuits become dominant. Burst errors cannot be corrected by conventional ECC. Thus the SEC (Single Error Correction) mandatory in DDR5 cannot recover soft errors.

articleTitle: Single-Event Effects Test Analysis of the ISL73148SEH Precision SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper will present data on destructive and non-destructive single-event effects (SEE) on the Intersil ISL73148SEH 8-channel high precision 14-bit, 900/480ksps SAR Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC).

articleTitle: SEE characterization of Microchip RTG4 FPGA SerDes block and GRLIB SpaceFibre IP core
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work presents an independent SEE characterization of the on-chip high-speed SerDes interface of Microchip’s RTG4 Flash-based FPGA while running GRLIB’s SpaceFibre IP core. The results obtained show an overall SEE rate of $2.4\times 10^{-5}$ and 6.4$\times 10^{-6}$ events/device/day for typical GEO and LEO orbits, respectively, and an average auto-recoverable rate of the GRLIB’s SpaceFibre IP core of 94%.

articleTitle: DDR3 SDRAM Stuck/Weak Bit Studies and Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper presents the results of DDR3 SDRAM stuck/weak bit studies from HI, TID, Neutron, Proton and temperature tests. The objectives include identifying reasonable engineering solutions to either screen or mitigate the stuck/weak bit for space applications.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Characterization Induced by Heavy Ions in 65-nm PLL
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper presents the characterization of the single event effect on a Radiation-Hardened Phase-Locked Loop (RHPLL) designed with a commercial 65nm bulk CMOS technology. The RHPLL guarantees the less than 280ps timing error, which is the difference between the nominal and the fluctuated output clock frequency due to SETs. Also, the RHPLL involves an additional function. If the period deviation continues for a while (long-term period deviation), the lock detector provides ‘0’ level pulse to support applications that use the absolute position of the clock edge. The long-term period deviation is characterized, and its cross-section is estimated by circuit simulations. The cross-section is verified by heavy ion test.

articleTitle: The HollandPTC R&D proton beam line for radiation hardness tests in space application
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: HollandPTC is the proton therapy centre based in Delft, the Netherlands. Within the R&D framework of HollanPTC, a feasibility study to assess the usability of the experimental proton area for Radiation Hardness Assurance tests for space applications was carried out in collaboration with ESA.

articleTitle: Alpha Particle- and Neutron-Induced Single-Event Effects in COTS Power FETS
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Alpha particles are one of the most abundant species in the space radiation environment, whereas neutrons are the main component of the radiation field on Earth. Few studies have been published for alpha particle- and neutron-induced Single-Event Effects (SEEs) in UMOSFETs, the current main candidate to supplant the traditional DMOSFET technology, and in the state-of-the-art GaN-on-Si HEMTs. In this work, experimental results of SEEs induced by an<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">241</sup> Am alpha particle source and quasi mono-energetic fast neutrons provided by a Deuteron-Tritium (DT) neutron generator in Si-containing COTS power FETs are presented. By comparing the SEE response of a DMOSFET and UMOSFET under alpha particle irradiation, the main aspects of the ion-induced charge collection mechanisms in a UMOSFET are investigated. The DT neutron-induced SEE responses of DMOSFET, UMOSFET, and GaN-on-Si HEMT are compared to the charge spectrum of a fully depleted silicon surface barrier detector.

articleTitle: Mitigation and Recovery of Single Event Effects in RTG4™ Transceiver Links Using SpaceFibre
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: SpaceFibre (ECSS-E-ST-50-11C) is a very high-performance, high-reliability and high-availability network technology specifically designed to meet the needs of space applications. It requires serial transceivers for implementation. The Microchip RTG4™ FPGA is equipped with 24 serial transceivers, each capable of supporting rates up to 3.125 Gbit/s. STAR-Dundee provides SpaceFibre communication IPs optimized for deployment on RTG4 FPGAs. Multiple lanes can be grouped to achieve aggregate bandwidths up to 25 Gbit/s. In this paper we present the results of radiation tests examining heavy-ion single event effect behavior of the serial transceivers used on the RTG4 FPGA while implementing SpaceFibre data links. We study both the native upset rates of the RTG4 transceivers and the resulting SpaceFibre link error rates. Results show that the use of SpaceFibre mitigates the effects of radiation allowing to create reliable links in harsh conditions.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Simulation Methodology for Ionizing Radiation Effect in Ultra-scaled SOI FinFETs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work proposes a 3D TID effect simulation methodology for sub-22-nm node SOI FinFETs. The method captures the S/D-induced non-uniform charge generation under irradiation, providing physical insights into the TID effect’s mechanism in ultra-scaled transistors.

articleTitle: Characterization of Radiation Tolerance of Bipolar Transistor with Al2O3 Dielectric at Different Dose Rates
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The radiation response of specially designed bipolar Darlington transistors with $Al_{2}O_{3}$-based dielectric after $^{60}$Co gamma-ray irradiation at various dose rates have been examined in this paper as a function of total dose. The base current sensitive to irradiation increases linearly with dose, dependent of the bias conditions and thickness of dielectric. According to the experimental results, it is shown that $Al_{2}O_{3}$ as a promising dielectric material may be achievable to resist the ionizing dose radiation for a bipolar transistor. Additionally, an enhanced effect occurring when the dose rate decreases is discussed with respect to interface traps buildup near the interfacial $SiO_{2}/Si$ structure. This suggests that reducing the thickness of the interfacial $SiO_{2}$ layer near the interface or increasing electron traps may be benefit to improve the enhanced low dose rate sensitivity (ELDRS) tolerance.

articleTitle: Electron beam characterization and first experimental results for the laser wake field accelerator for radiation to electronics effects applications
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A new source of relativistic electrons based on laser wakefield acceleration has been recently built and commissioned at ELI-Beamlines user facility. This platform is proposed for the experimental study of radiation to electronics effects for components and devices dimensioned to laboratory and low Earth orbit applications, such as picosatellite class spacecrafts, e.g. CubeSat. The device is configured to represent energy range of relativistic electrons trapped in the Van Allen radiation belts, 0.1 – 10 MeV, and to study the effects of ultra-high dose rates radiation. The developed instrument includes a permanent magnet dipole electron beam spectrometer with luminescent screen for on-line beam parameters monitoring and vacuum to air interface. The electron beam acceleration experiment for up to 10 MeV energies have been performed using a nitrogen gas target. The generated electron beam has been used for the electronic device irradiation experiments. The profile of the beam, energy and dose imparted per laser pulse have been measured to evaluate efficiency of the device. The beam characterization technique has designed using the FLUKA Monte Carlo code. KE spectrometer is calibrated with conventional LINAC source of electrons.

articleTitle: Comparative of proton radiation data for 28 nm Zynq-7000 SoC
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this work, two irradiation campaigns performed over the Xilinx Zynq 7000 SoC in two different irradiation facilities are presented and compared. The same experiments were tested in CNA, Spain, with protons of 15 MeV and in PSI, Switzerland, with protons of 230 MeV. The experiments in both campaigns tested the programmable logic and the processing system present in the Zynq-7000 SoC. Experimental results show that the behavior of the two main parts of the system differ for the two energy ranges used.

articleTitle: Single Event Transient Sensitivity Analysis and Worst-Case Test Vector Identification for ASICs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A new methodolgy for SET sensitivity measurements is proposed from cell to circuit level. A new approach is also introduced to analyze SET enhancement in the circuit to identify the worst-case test vector.

articleTitle: Effect of Heavy Ion Irradiation on SiC MOSFET Dynamic Parameter
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: To evaluate the effect of heavy-ion irradiation on SiC MOSFET dynamic parameters, the gate charges of SiC MOSFET were tested. The change of the gate charges induced by heavy-ion was simulated by TCAD The gate-to-source charges QGS increased and the gate-to-drain charges QGD decreased. It was concluded that the change of gate charge was related to the acceptor traps induced by heavy ions in the JFET neck region. The traps induced by heavy-ion would degrade reliability of devices.

articleTitle: Heavy-ion and proton characterization of AMD 7nm Versal™ multicore scalar processing system (PS)
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper presents the single event response of Xilinx’s 7nm Versal ACAP dual R5 and dual A72 ARM core processor system (PS) for Space applications. The PS was evaluated using Xilinx’s System Validation Tool (SVT) design suite. Accelerated particle beam test of a XCVC1902 device was performed using the heavy-ion source at Berkeley BASE and proton sources at Crocker Nuclear Laboratory (CNL) and Triumf. More than 10 million designs exercising all the PS power domains were generated during the test. The PS single-event results are presented and categorized in terms of detectability and correctability. No SEL was observed in the PS up to a LET of 80 $\mathrm{MeV}-\mathrm{cm}^{2} / \mathrm{mg}$, 110° C and VCCmax values. With all PS safety mechanisms enabled, beam test results show that the overall PS SEFI rate in GEO is 0.16 SEFI per year and 1 SEFI per year (at 500 km and 51.6° inclination) in LEO. Also, no uncorrectable events were observed in the PS caches and RAMs.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose Tolerance of LoRa Wireless Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The response of several Long-range (LoRa) wireless devices to total ionizing dose has been assessed using <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co gamma-rays. We found that the radiation tolerance of the different tested devices is comprised between 220 and 1600 Gy.

articleTitle: Demonstration of ZES’ LDAP (Latchup Detection and Protection) Enabling a Commercial-Off-the-Shelf FPGA for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the performance of Latchup Detection and Protection (LDAP), a product of Zero-Error Systems (ZES), in protecting a target chip from Single-Event Latchup (SEL). A pulsed laser is used to induce SELs in a Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and LDAP is implemented to protect the FPGA by removing the induced SELs. Laser tests are performed on two identical FPGA samples, one with LDAP and the other without LDAP. After laser tests, the FPGA with LDAP still operates well whereas the FPGA without LDAP is partially damaged. The experiment shows that when an SEL happens, LDAP detects the SEL at different loading scenarios within 5μs, and removes the SEL successfully thereafter. There is no false detection observed during the tests. As compared to conventional current limiters, LDAP has a much faster response and protects COTS FPGAs from SELs more effectively.

articleTitle: Proton-induced MBU Effects in Real-time Operating System on Embedded Soft Processor
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, we perform an evaluation of the impact of radiation-induced micro-architectural faults affecting the Microblaze soft-processor running a Real-Time Operating System. Fault injection campaigns with a proton-radiation test fault model are presented.

articleTitle: An SRAM-based Multiple Event Upsets Detection Method for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work proposes a new way to deal with the Multiple Event Upsets in SRAM memories for space applications. The method consists of spatially interleaving a memory plan with a network of memory radiation detectors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Efficiency and Utilization with SRAM Dosimetry for Single-Event Effect Evaluation under Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: For the first time, we have proposed a quantitative correction factor $(Q_{\text {crit}\_\text{eff}})$ ratio model as a way to select SRAMs for reference dosimeters. In order to improve the accuracy of $(Q_{\text {crit}\_\text{eff}})$ model, reverse engineer-level SRAM physical structure analysis was used to precisely extract device parameters such as cell active area and cell MOSFETs’ array in the cell region, well tap distance, and well depth. The quantitative correction factor $(Q_{\text {crit}\_\text{eff}})$ ratio was calculated in consideration of the geometrical effect with the device parameters for SRAM sensitivity of single event upset (SEU). As a result, using the $(Q_{\text {crit}\_\text{eff}})$ structures of SRAM, FIT ratio provides higher accurate than that of conventional critical charge ratio. Furthermore, for the selected SRAM, SEU dependency on proton energy and device package characteristic is analyzed which shows SEU generation at 0-MeV and proton direct ionization (PDI) effect for reference data when using our SRAM dosimeter under the condition of below 100-MeV. Finally, efficiency of using reference SRAM dosimeter for single event effect (SEE) evaluation is verified at test for radiation effect of SiC power diodes by providing fluence of proton for single event burnout (SEB) evaluation.

articleTitle: Irradiation-and Bias-Stress-Induced Charge Trapping and Gate Leakage in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Effects of proton irradiation and bias-stress are evaluated for the degradation and gate leakage of commercial AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. These devices are sensitive to bias stress and robust to proton irradiation. Gate leakage is shown to increase significantly with short-term high-current stress and/or high-fluence proton irradiation.

articleTitle: Validation of a new 60 MeV proton beam-line for radiation hardness testing
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A 60 MeV proton beam-line has been developed in Nice, France, in collaboration with the Centre National d’Etudes Spatiales (CNES). Experimental results are presented here to validate the beam-line for radiation hardness testing.

articleTitle: Ionizing Radiation Hardness Characterization of GaN HEMTs Depends on the Radiation Source
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work presents a radiation effects comparison in a COTS GaN HEMT observed when this transistor is irradiated with a 10 keV X-ray and a 1.25 MeV γ-ray electromagnetic radiation. The results indicate that these two sources may affect this device differently.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects Characterization and System Architecture Options for the 7nm Snapdragon SA8155P Automotive Grade System on Chip (SoC)
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The SA8155PSoC is a complex heterogeneous computational platform with CPUs, GPU, DSPs and NPU. The SA8155P is a 7 TOPS/7 Watts capable AI/ML platform and as such represents a game changing breakthrough in terms computational power for space applications. We characterize the TID and SEE effects of the Qualcomm SA8155P Automotive grade SoC. Individual sub-system testing as well as application specific full device testing was conducted. We also discuss the commercial and automotive recovery mechanisms that are available with the SA8155PSoC generation and how those can form the basis for resilient architecture options for use in future space missions.

articleTitle: TCAD Calibrated SEE Fault Model Validated with Beam Results for a 12nm D Flip-Flop.
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A simple simulation-based approach to accurately estimating the single even effect (SEE) cross section of a standard cell library Flip-Flop is presented. A SPICE level model of charge injection is calibrated to 3D mixed mode technology computer aided design (TCAD) device simulations. The TCAD results for charge collection by distance from the fin are then used to estimate the sensitive area of the Flip-Flop circuit at a given LET. We show good agreement between the circuit simulations and measured results.

articleTitle: Combined Neutron and TID Results of the Intersil ISL70100SEH 40V Current Sense Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We report the combined results of the ISL70100SEH 40V current sense amplifier after exposure to $5 \times 10^{11}, 2 \times 10^{12}$, and $1 \times 10^{13}$ neutrons/$\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ followed by 100 krad(Si) HDR total ionizing dose.

articleTitle: Ultra-High-Energy Heavy Ion Induced Single Event Effect of TSV-Based 3D Integrated SOI SRAM Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The single event upset of TSV-based four-tier 3D SRAM circuits is investigated through experimental method with ultra-high-energy heavy ions and the upset cross-section exhibits strong relationship on the tier positions, range and incident angles.

articleTitle: SEE Test Results for COTS High Speed LVDS Driver and Receivers
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Single event effects results from heavy ions are presented for COTS LVDS High Speed Differential Driver and Receiver ICs at room and elevated, 75°C.

Author Keywords: LVDS Low Voltage Differential Signaling technology

articleTitle: Radiation and its Effects on monolithic GaN integrated half-bridge for dc-dc converters
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper first presents the successful co-integration of high-performance Schottky barrier diodes and depletion-mode HEMTs on a p-GaN HEMT-based 200 V GaN-on-SOI smart power integrated circuit. The addition of these components enables the design of chips with extended functionality and increased performance that takes monolithically-integrated GaN power ICs one step further.The built circuit features all blocks needed to make a fully GaN integrated half-bridge 200V, 10A and 5MHz switching.The circuit has been tested against heavy-ions & total ionizing dose in order to survive harsh space environments. The results presented in this document allow to claim that the technology is per nature radiation hard for space applications. This achievement paves the way towards smaller and more efficient DC/DC converters and Point-of-Load converters for space.

articleTitle: Micro-latch and Single Event Upset phenomena observed during accelerated atmospheric neutron testing of 40-90 nm Commercial Off The Shelf Static Random Access Memories
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper summarizes observations of micro-SEL phenomena during the SEU testing of sub 100 nm COTS SRAMs with an accelerated atmospheric neutron spectra. SEU statistics are compared with historic data to demonstrate there is not a potential SEU increased susceptibility for modern COTS SRAMs however the static test method may have displayed characteristics i.e. micro-latches that may not be visible from a pseudo-static test. The SEU cross sections demonstrates the essential requirement to continue to test SRAMs for their responses to atmospheric neutrons particularly those which will be used within critical applications e.g. flight avionics.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Terrestrial Neutron Induced Failures in Commercial Silicon and Silicon Carbide Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Accelerated neutron tests on Si and SiC power MOSFETs at different temperatures were performed at ChipIr facility (Didcot, UK). The results show a strong correlation between the temperature dependence of the avalanche voltage and that of the neutron failure rate.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion and Proton Induced SEUs in Very Deep Sub-Micron Technologies
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Three deep submicron devices have been tested with heavy ions, low energy protons, and high energy protons in the frame of a study about Single Event Upset induced by Low Energy Protons (LEP). The test data are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Methodology for Feedback Loop Detection and Automatic Voter Placement in TMR Netlists
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, we present an algorithm for detecting feedback loops in sequential digital circuits as well as an algorithm for optimally inserting majority voters on essential circuit nodes which are vulnerable to Single Event Upsets (SEUs). In conjunction with triplication tools, this approach is able to automate a full radiation hardening flow strategy for complex digital designs, resulting in a Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) RTL design with optimal voter placement. The proposed algorithms are formally defined and explained with example circuits.

articleTitle: TID and SEE characterization of Microchip PolarFire® SoC FPGA
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The TID response of Microchip 28 nm PolarFire<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> SoC SONOS-based FPGA is characterized using gamma ray. The Single-Event response of PolarFire<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> SoC is characterized using heavy ion and 64 MeV proton. The SONOS configuration cell is SEU immune and the TID exceeds 100krad (SiO2) due to the SONOS technology and the design of the configuration cell of PolarFire<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> SoC FPGA.

articleTitle: Short-term trap decay in a cryogenically irradiated charge-coupled device
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A CCD was irradiated cryogenically, and the trap pumping technique was used to monitor the evolution of the radiation induced traps. An unexpected trap was found which decays with a time constant of 3-4 hours.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion Single Event Effects Measurements of the 512Mb ISSI Version F SDRAM
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Heavy ion single-event measurements on 512Mb ISSI synchronous dynamic random-access memory (SDRAM) version F are reported. Heavy ion susceptibility to single event latchup (SEL), single bit upsets (SBUs), and single effect functional interrupts (SEFIs) were investigated.

articleTitle: Soft Error Reliability Prediction of SRAM-based FPGA Designs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We developed a tool for the reliability analysis of SEU effects on the configuration memory of Xilinx Zynq SRAM-based FPGAs. A proton radiation test campaign on different TMR layouts demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: A RISC-V System-on-Chip with Embedded Adaptive Power–Performance–Fault-Tolerance Hardware
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This article presents a 28 nm FD-SOI RISC-V System-on-Chip with integrated Dynamic Voltage, Forward Body-Bias and Frequency Scaling scheme for adaptive radiation hardening according to the radiation environment estimates computed from the embedded radiation monitors.

articleTitle: Demonstrating Risk-Driven and Mitigation-Focused Single-Event Functional Interrupt Testing
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Motivations for developing SEE tests around risk and mitigation are described. Test data are presented where SEFI testing of flash memories produced granular SEFI data to calculate the impact of mitigations on science data loss.

articleTitle: X-ray Radiation Effects Assessment on NVMs manufactured in ST 90 nm BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The Total Ionizing Dose effects induced by X-ray radiation were investigated on different types of BCD Non-Volatile Memories based on antifuse elements, phase change materials or single poly floating gate up to 1000 Gy dose.

Author Keywords: Anti-fuse High Density One Time Programmable Memories

articleTitle: Threshold Voltage Shift of SiC MOSFETs Induced by High Temperature Gate Bias and Total Ionizing Dose
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: To study whether the threshold voltage shifts of SiC MOSFETs caused by high temperature gate bias (HTGB) were affected by total ionizing dose (TID) irradiation and vice versa, the threshold voltage shifts of Silicon Carbide (SiC) Metal Oxide Semiconductor Filed Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) induced by HTGB and TID were tested. HTGB caused positive shift under positive gate bias, and negative shift under negative gate bias. The threshold voltage shift post-irradiation were mainly controlled by the radiation-induced oxide trapped charges. The conclusion was that the near-interface traps (NITs) and the radiation-induced oxide trapped charges were independent of each other and may cause threshold voltage shift independently or together. The threshold voltage shifts were the function of TID, gate bias and temperature.

articleTitle: NOEL-V FT and GRSCRUB IP: Fault Tolerance Characterization of a Complex System-on-Chip on Xilinx Kintex UltraScale FPGA
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work presents the SEE fault tolerance characterization of the NOEL-V FT RISC-V processor IP core combined with the GRSCRUB FPGA supervisor protection on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale FPGA. Additionally, a distributed TMR synthesis strategy is applied to enhance the resilience of the system against SEE. Results from a proton beam irradiation show the efficiency of the NOEL-V fault tolerance features in correcting single errors and preventing error accumulation, the GRSCRUB’s advanced capability of error detection and correction, and the masking effects of the distributed TMR method.

articleTitle: Redundant Portable Multi-Threading for Soft Error Mitigation on Multicore Systems on Chip
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work presents a software technique to protect commercial multicore microprocessors against soft errors induced by ionizing radiation. Traditional software redundancy techniques introduce important time overheads, which limits feasibility in advanced critical electronic systems. In our approach, critical computation is spread over the different microprocessor cores by using redundant bare-metal threads. This way, software redundancy can be applied to COTS devices without involving high performance penalties. The proposed technique was evaluated in a low-cost single board computer (Raspberry Pi 4) under neutron irradiation. The results show that the multi-threaded technique can detect and correct single event faults without inquiring in performance overheads.

articleTitle: Soft-error Tolerance by Guard-Gate Structures on Flip-Flops in 22/65 nm FD-SOI Technologies
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We evaluated soft-error tolerance by heavy-ion irradiation test on three-types of flip-flops (FFs) called the standard FF (STDFF), the dual feedback recovery FF (DFRFF), and the DFRFF with long delay (DFRFFLD) in 22/65 nm FDSOI technologies. The guard-gate (GG) structure in the DFRFF mitigates soft errors. An SET pulse is removed by the C-element with the signal delayed by the GG structure. DFRFFLD increases the GG delay by adding two more inverters as delay elements. We investigate the effectiveness of GG structure in 22 nm and 65 nm. In 22 nm, Kr (40.3 MeV-$cm^{\mathbf{2}}$/mg) irradiation tests revealed that DFRFFLD has sufficient soft-error tolerance in outer space. In 65 nm, the relationship between GG delay and CS reveals the GG delay time which no error was observed under Kr irradiation.

articleTitle: TID effects on a 110 nm CMOS technology for fully depleted monolithic sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of ionizing radiation on NMOS and PMOS transistors belonging to a 110 nm CMOS technology used in the design of fully depleted sensors for applications to particle and astro-particle physics and medical radio-diagnostic equipment. The work is focused in particular on electronic noise, also as a tool for studying the degradation process induced by total ionizing dose (TID) in the analog performance of the technology. The characterization results can be leveraged for the design of low noise, rad-hard front-end processors for monolithic sensors in a 110 nm process.

articleTitle: Pulse Quenching Effect Characterized by Inverter Chains under Heavy-ion Irradiation in 28-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: As the device keeps scaling down, single-event charge sharing effect becomes more significant, thus making pulse quenching effect a great concern. In this paper, The pulse quenching effect on single-event transients (SETs) in 28-nm twin-well CMOS technology is characterized. Four groups of heavy ion experiments, with two types of particles and two strike angles, on two different layout-customized inverter chains were carried out for the characterization. The experimental results show that the pulse-quenching in the 28-nm technology has a significant mitigation effect on SETs, and the degree of influence is mainly determined by the linear-energy-transfer (LET) and the angle of the striking particle.

articleTitle: Radiation test methodology for avionics equipment
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Neutron irradiations at board/equipment level have been performed on avionics equipment, in order to assess its radiation behavior and to verify the efficiency of monitoring to detect SEE impact. The methodology is presented, as well as the results obtained at the TRIUMF facility.

articleTitle: Characterization of Radiation Hardness of Organic Transistors for a Flexible X-Ray Imager
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We present the characterization of complementary p-type and n-type organic transistors in terms of X-ray radiation hardness. These transistors are fabricated as the backplane of an array of photo-conductive pixels based on perovskites for direct X-ray imaging on flexible substrates. Experimental results show that irradiation up to 1 kGy produces negligible effects (a tolerable maximum shift of the transistor threshold voltage of about 40% right after exposure, which is almost completely recovered after 24 hours at rest).

articleTitle: Impact of Tap Cell on Single Event Transient in 28-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In advanced integrated circuit (IC) technologies at the 28-nm node and below, tap cells are used for well and substrate contact in actual VLSI design in pursuit of higher device density. To investigate the difference in SET sensitivity between different placements in designs using tap cells as well and substrate contacts, in this paper, SET vulnerability of inverter cells placed at different distances to tap cells are studied. Results show that in 28-nm CMOS technology, n-MOSFETs are not sensitive to the variation in placement, whereas the p-MOSFET shows regular variations in SET widths if placed with gradual changes in distance from the tap cell. Therefore, the parasitic bipolar amplification effect in the p-MOSFET is also studied. It is shown that this effect is the main reason for the variation in SET sensitivity in p-MOSFETs with different placements. This study provides guidance to circuit designers on how to determine the physical location of standard cells during the large-scale advanced process circuit design.

articleTitle: TID&SEE characterization for a Dual channel Ka-band capable 12 GSps DAC (April 2022)
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The EV12DD700 is a Ka-band capable 12-bit Digital-to-Analog converter, 12 GSps, synthetizing signals over 25GHz without up conversion. A TID test and a SEE have been performed to validate its suitability to severe space environment.

articleTitle: Compendium of SEE and TID Test Results for DDR4 SDRAM memories
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper reports the results and analysis of single event effects (SEE) tests and total ionizing dose (TID) on DDR4-SDRAM memories. The compendium covers five DDR4-SDRAM references from different manufactures tested in the frame of CNES studies.

articleTitle: Investigation of Leakage Current Degradation Mechanism under Heavy Ions Irradiation in SiC Junction Barrier Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, stacking faults in the epitaxial layer of SiC JBS diode were detected after heavy ions irradiation. Based on this result, a new mechanism of leakage current degradation in SiC junction barrier Schottky diodes under heavy ions irradiation was investigated by experiments and simulations, which is related to stacking faults induced by massive electron-hole pairs recombination under irradiation.

articleTitle: Single Event Effects Results of Rad Hard Gate Drivers RIC7S113 and RIC74424
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Heavy Ion SEE test results of rad hard gate drivers RIC78113 and RIC74424 are summarized. Results include reanalysis of existing data and new results. New results include high resolution SET events not previously reported.

articleTitle: Energy and beam delivery upgrade of the TOP-IMPLART proton linear accelerator
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This contribution describes the energy upgrade to 71 MeV of the TOP-IMPLART linear accelerator of ENEA Frascati Research Centre, its final layout with a foreseen maximum available proton energy of 110 MeV and an active scanning delivery system. While the accelerator is specifically designed for radiotherapy, it has already been applied as a radiation source for different applications, including characterization of electronic components radiation tolerance. Once fully commissioned, the TOP-IMPLART accelerator will constitute a significant addition to ENEA portfolio of already available radiation facilities (gamma and X rays, neutrons, electrons).

articleTitle: Soft-Error Analysis of Different Magnetic Storage Cells based on Spin Orbit Torque
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Soft-error of the three-terminal magnetic storage cells including spin-orbit torque (SOT) and voltage-gated SOT was simulated by macrospin models. Magnetic storage cells were vulnerable to radiation current, leading to magnetization dynamics changed during relaxed time.

articleTitle: Development of a Fully-distributed Stretcher-based Single Event Monitor for BCD Digital Designs
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A fully integrated and distributed Soft Error sensitive design has been proposed based on stretcher architecture. The preliminary characterization results under alpha particles source focusing on the effect of sensor filling elements will be reported.

articleTitle: Single Event Effect and Total Ionizing Dose Performance at High and Low Dose Rate of a 16 Bit Digital-to-Analog Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A Digital to Analog Converter (DAC) was evaluated by using high energy proton and high/low dose rate <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co. The DAC remains functional up to 40krad(Si). A SEFI event was observed during proton testing.

articleTitle: Predictive study on a bipolar operational amplifier behaviour under gamma and protons radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A successful predictive analysis, based on archival data, for one bipolar operational amplifier is presented in this work. The model has been evaluated crosschecking with the results from new TID and DD radiation test campaigns.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Google’s Tensor Processing Units to High-Energy, Mono-Energetic, and Thermal Neutrons
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We investigate the reliability of Tensor Processing Units executing 2D-3D convolutions and eight CNNs to high-energy, mono-energetic, and thermal neutrons. Despite the high error rate, most neutron-induced errors do not change the CNNs detection/classification.

articleTitle: Radiation test flux selection methodology to optimize SEE observability on systems with different operating modes
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Systems and Systems on Chip (SoCs) under radiation can have complex failure modes with different probabilities. A system may have, due to its different modalities of operation and depending on the selected test flux, a probability that the failure with the highest probability of occurrence masks the others, preventing them from being detected. Flux selection becomes a key parameter in system-level testing to increase the observability of such events and prevent them from remaining hidden. The inability to detect and identify these events could lead to unexpected failures during operation. This work proposes a methodology to evaluate the degree of observability of low probability fault modes by varying the flux and demonstrates its validity through measurements.

articleTitle: Proton and X-rays radiation effects on Silicon Photomultipliers
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) are single-photon sensitive large-area detectors widely used in many applications. Among them, they are used in several radiation-harsh applications, like high-energy physics and experiments in space, where they receive a significant radiation dose. The effect of ionizing and nonionizing radiation dose on their performance is very interesting for those applications. In this contribution we irradiated several silicon photomultipliers technologies produced at FBK with 74MeV protons and with 40 keVX-rays (up to to 100kGy dose in silicon). We monitored the reverse current after each proton or X-ray irradiation step. We also characterized the SiPMs functionally after the irradiation and after few weeks of room temperature annealing. We studied the main degradation effects and the main difference in the functional performances modification among the SiPM technologies. Having a complete knowledge of the internal structures of the SiPMs and being able to compare directly the effects on performances degradation of different SiPM technologies is very interesting for a future development of a more radiation-tolerant SiPM technology.

articleTitle: Pulsed X-rays Induced Single Event Effects in Si, SiC and GaN Technologies
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Alternative SEE test methods are increasingly sought after. This work is a contribution to the use of a pulsed X-rays beam. The main objective was to evaluate the parameters leading to the correlation between pulsed X-rays, broadbeam heavy ions, and laser pulses on wide bandgap component technologies (SiC and GaN). Indeed, these technologies can present preparation issues and pulsed X-rays can be an interesting solution to overcome them. Comparisons were also performed to study non-destructive and destructive events with different levels of package thinning of the devices allowing to rule on the capacity of pulsed X-rays to cross these packages.

articleTitle: Upscreening of Infineon Hall Effect Sensors for the MMX rover locomotion subsystem
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The MMX (Martian Moons eXploration mission), conducted by JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) aims to explore both Mars moons Phobos and Deimos. This mission is supported by a small rover intended to land on Phobos, jointly developed by CNES (Centre national d’études spatiales) and DLR (German Aerospace Center). An essential part of this rover is the locomotion subsystem, which includes several sensors and eight motors actuating four legs, and the four wheels mount on them.. In each of the BLDC (Brushless DC) motors are three industrial Hall effect sensors mounted, used for incremental position sensing and motor commutation in parallel. Smaller form factor and high accuracy are two key requirements for the selection of the Infinion TLE4945L Hall effect sensors. Since the motors are not located in the insulated inner compartment of the rover, they must withstand extreme temperature ranges of $-75^{\circ} C$ to $+85^{\circ} C$ (non operational). This goes beyond the temperature range of industrial electronics and space grade electronics. Therefore, an up-screening campaign was performed, where the radiation and the temperature performance of the Hall effect sensors were measured. This paper highlights the most important results of the conducted tests.

articleTitle: Australia’s External Ion Microbeam Irradiation Facility For Space Radiation Effects Testing
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The new external ion microbeam irradiation facility at the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology organisation (ANSTO) Centre for Accelerator Science (CAS) is presented. The CAS Heavy Ion Microprobe on the 10 MV ANTARES accelerator was recently upgraded with an enclosed chamber in air at ambient temperature and pressure. The chamber is the first one in Australia dedicated to the testing of electronic components, particularly Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS), for space qualification with ion microbeams. Post commissioning, GEANT4 Monte Carlo simulation capabilities were established to evaluate the Linear Energy Transfer (LET) and dose rate profile for ions. Proton beams with energy up to 9 MeV were simulated while propagating through the chamber and the COTS chips of interest. The encapsulation was etched to a minimal thickness to allow ions penetration into the silicon sensitive volume. Irradiation with 9 MeV protons were performed on a large number of COTS, allowing the investigation of Total Ionizing Dose (TID) and Single Event Effects (SEE) were investigated. The facility, the GEANT4 simulation, the in-house readout system, and the preliminary results are discussed in this paper. Our latest etching capability for removal of the surface encapsulation is also presented, together with material characterisation of the samples by scanning electron microscopy and energy dispersive spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory Comparison in Dosimetry between four EN ISO/IEC 17025 Accredited European Irradiation Facilities: ESA-ESTEC, RadLab (CNA-ALTER), Seibersdorf Laboratories and TRAD
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Interlaboratory comparison are obligatory for accredited entities EN ISO/IEC 17025. Four accredited European laboratories have compared their dosimetry measurement systems with respect to calibration standards, validating the dosimetry procedures and practices.

articleTitle: Observation of lower hardness factor for displacement damage induced by high-energy electrons
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Experimental measurements of electron displacement damage at the CLEAR facility at CERN were performed on several diodes previously calibrated with neutrons and protons. The idea behind the study was to assess whether the facility can be used as an alternative for displacement damage qualification to neutron and proton irradiations. In the last case, the foreseen advantages are a fast test, thanks to the high electron fluxes available, and of a lower activation of the test samples that enables accessing them for post-test characterization straight after the test. The experimental measurements on two different types of diodes, both previously calibrated against neutrons and protons, resulted in the observation of ~2 lower damage than expected. Monte-Carlo (MC) simulations are used to understand whether the lower hardness factor observed is due to (i) electron being less damaging than previously thought or (ii) specific beam conditions encountered during this test. The non-ionising energy loss (NIEL) and hardness factor determined from the MC tools when the energy threshold for primary knocked-on atoms is 21 eV are typically lower than those previously established. However, they are still higher than the experimental results. Calculations with higher energy threshold show that the electron NIEL and hardness factor would further decrease. However, this would require setting threshold in excess of 100 eV.

articleTitle: Constructing Application-level GPU Error Rate Model with Neutron Irradiation Experiment
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work explores GPU application factors that dominantly characterize SDC and DUE cross sections obtained by neutron irradiation experiments. We evaluate correlation coefficients between the cross sections and application metrics obtained from profiler outputs and fault injection results. Experimental results with six applications show that “warps per block” is a primary factor for both SDC and DUE. The DUE cross section modeling is improved by the secondary factor of L2 hit rate.

articleTitle: Single Event Upset sensitivity analyses and prediction based on methodology from design to operational risks
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work presents a methodology to analyze and estimate the soft error rate of a digital device for aircraft and automotive applications. This methodology is based on simulation platforms relating to the SET/SEU simulation at cells and circuits levels (RAPTOR), and physical atmospheric cosmic-ray showers simulations (ATMOS CORE). The methodology is applied on the SRAM cell of the Microchip Rad-Tolerant product SAM3X8RT, considering realistic flights/ground environments for quiet solar conditions and extreme solar event. Results demonstrate the interest of coupled approaches and show the importance to consider realistic flight and physical model to assess SERs.

articleTitle: Heavy Ion Induced SEU and MBU Sensitivity of 3D NAND Flash Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The use of 3D integration technologies in future satellites is increasingly considered in order to obtain better performance gains. Testability, reliability assessment and radiation resistance are important issues for space applications. It has been shown that 3D architectures give birth to enhanced Single Event Effects sensitivities, which may need to be assessed in different ways than their planar predecessors.In this work, the heavy ions induced SEU and MBU sensitivities of commercially off the shelf (COTS) 3D NAND flash memories are investigated through experimental characterization and compared to Monte-Carlo simulations performed thanks to the TRADCARE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">©</sup> software. Dedicated Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) imagery was used to propose a highly representative model of the memory array giving good confidence in these simulations.

articleTitle: Preliminary study of electronics reliability in ITER neutron environment
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We validated a method for predicting the Soft Error Rate (SER) in the WEST tokamak operated with deuterium plasmas, and we applied it to predict the SER in the ITER tokamak operated with deuterium-tritium plasmas.

articleTitle: Spatial Dependence of Single Event Transients in Wide Bandgap Materials Photodiodes Probed by Pulsed Laser, Pulsed X-Rays and Heavy Ions Microbeam
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this work, we report on the investigation of the spatial dependence of single event transients observed in wide bandgap semiconductor based components (gallium nitride and silicon carbide), generated by femtosecond pulsed laser, pulsed X-rays and heavy ions microbeam. We evidence a strong spatial dependence of the amount of collected charges as a function of the distance to contacts. Similar variations are observed among all three tests means.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Analysis of Total Ionizing Dose in Microelectronics
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Supervised deep learning is a subset of machine learning (ML) that allows for the development of phenomenological models based on measured observations through layered artificial neurons. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is one model typically used in image recognition that allows for classifying behavior in discrete sets or enabling regression analysis. This work demonstrates a one-dimensional CNN to analyze irradiated commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) electronics. COTS microcontroller units (MCU) were irradiated with 10 keV X-rays, and CNN models were trained on the resulting internally generated noise signatures from the clock module. As a result, the MCUs are accurately classified as either fresh or dosed, and the total ionizing dose (TID) is predictable through a regression model. This approach allows for part dosimetry and in situ device health monitoring without additional components.

articleTitle: Fault Propagation in Microprocessors with Configurable Cache Memory
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) microprocessors are attractive in applications with radiation requirements because they have better capabilities than radiation hardened microprocessors. This work reports the single event functional interrupt SEFI cross-section $\sigma$ of a configurable single-core microprocessor. The relationship between the performance of the software algorithms and their SEFI cross sections is reported. During irradiation, the cache configuration was changed between on and off states. When the cache was activated the SEFI $\sigma$ increased, but the work completed by the processor before a SEFI was at least $1.5 \times$ greater compared to the work completed when cache was off. The software algorithms with the highest SEFI cross section had the lowest time performance gain when cache memory was on, and they had the lowest percentage of L1 instruction cache hits.

articleTitle: Impact of the use of new environment models on the project specification: GREEN, SAPPHIRE, AE9/AP9
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: A comparison between new radiation environment models (GREEN, AE9/AP9 and SAPPHIRE) and the current standards (AE8/AP8, IGE2006, ESP, CREME96) is performed. The study focuses on the impact of the use of these new models at component level: the comparison is made on the dose values as well as on the estimated SEE rates. The comparison is performed for several typical missions: GEO, LEO, MEO, EOR.

articleTitle: SEE Testing of COTS Microcontroller and Operational Amplifier in the Framework of the ESA CORHA Study
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We present SEE radiation test data of two commercial microcontroller and two commercial operational amplifier as part of the ESA CORHA study. The aim of the CORHA study is to investigate COTS components relevant for the space industry in general as well as for nanosatellites and CubeSat applications in particular. The ESA CORHA study uses TID and SEE radiation test data as a basis for formulating an ad-hoc RHA approach for COTS components.

articleTitle: The General Chairman’s Address : Welcome to the Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Radiation Effects on Components and Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: On behalf of the conference committee and the Radiation Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS) association, it is my great pleasure to present the Proceedings of RADECS 2022, which was held October 3-7, 2022 in the Palazzo del Cinema in the Lido Island, Venice, Italy.
